question: The National Population Policy 2000 (NPP-2000) set which of the following as its long-term demographic goal for India?

answers.text: Achieve a Total Fertility Rate (TFR) of 2.1 by 2010 to reach replacement-level fertility.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. NPP-2000 explicitly targets a TFR of 2.1 (replacement-level fertility) by 2010, along with 80% institutional delivery, universal immunisation, and reduction of IMR to below 30 per 1,000 live births.

answers.text: Achieve zero population growth by 2000 through mandatory sterilisation for all couples with more than two children.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. NPP-2000 explicitly abandoned coercive measures. It is a voluntary, rights-based framework. Zero population growth was not a stated goal — replacement-level fertility (TFR 2.1) was.

answers.text: Reduce the Crude Birth Rate to below 10 per 1,000 population by 2045.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. NPP-2000's demographic goal is expressed as a TFR target (2.1), not a CBR target. A CBR below 10 would be among the lowest in the world and was not stated in the policy.

answers.text: Stabilise population at 1 billion by limiting each state to a maximum of 2% annual growth rate.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. NPP-2000 does not impose state-level growth rate caps. Its strategy is voluntary fertility reduction through improved access to family planning services, education, and health care.

overallFeedback.feedback: NPP-2000 key target: TFR = 2.1 (replacement level) by 2010. The policy is voluntary and rights-based — not coercive. Remember this figure for MCQs: 2.1 is the replacement-level fertility threshold.
Well recalled. NPP-2000's long-term demographic goal is TFR of 2.1 (replacement-level fertility) by 2010, achieved through voluntary family planning.
